title: Total live-hypothesis attack sweep

overrides.note: The unrestricted polynomial transformer can first decide SAT and then emit a trivial low-treewidth answer; the useful route survives only in restricted descendants.
The unrestricted submodular transformer is solve-and-encode equivalent to the target theorem; no independent mechanism is isolated.
A polynomial transformer may decide SAT before outputting a trivial totally-unimodular system; extension-complexity attacks need a restricted lift class.
The unrestricted moment lift can hide the SAT decision in the transformer; constant-level hierarchy language alone does not remove circularity.
A finite local rewrite system can simulate general computation across many steps, so locality alone does not exclude a hidden universal solver.
Pure XOR cores are eliminated by design, while no explicit mixed residual family is yet proved to retain superlogarithmic width after the allowed preprocessing.
The interface-DAG language is not yet restrictive enough to prevent a node from denoting a globally hard function, so the claimed compression mechanism remains underspecified.
The standard SAT-to-conflict-graph reduction and first theta level fail to expose UNSAT on known hard regimes; only a genuinely new gap-producing compiler remains viable.
Exact verification does not imply existence of polynomial-bit rational certificates; conditioning and reconstruction margins remain indispensable.
Ordinary rational Gram factors do not form a complete certificate language for all rational PSD matrices; C011 had to replace the route by rational LDL certificates.
